title: Palmares and Zumbi: Doing It Again

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *volver a* + infinitive from B2 Unit 23: it means "to do again" and works in every tense, and with *no* it means "not ... again". The history of Palmares is a history of repeated events: expeditions that came back, a date remembered every year. Here *volver a* works on Palmares and Zumbi.

sections.title: volver a + infinitive
rows: Las autoridades volvieron a enviar tropas contra el quilombo.
Los habitantes del quilombo volvían a levantar sus casas.
imperfect: they used to rebuild their houses again
Cada 20 de noviembre se vuelve a recordar a Zumbi.
present: it is remembered again each year
Zumbi no volvió a aceptar la propuesta de paz.
with *no*: he did not accept it again

items.spanish: El ejército volvió a atacar el quilombo en 1694.
items.english: The army attacked the quilombo again in 1694.

items.spanish: Los fugitivos volvían a formar nuevas aldeas.
items.english: The fugitives formed new villages again.

items.spanish: Brasil no ha vuelto a vivir la esclavitud legal desde 1888.
items.english: Brazil has not had legal slavery again since 1888.

sections.content: Do not confuse *volver a* + infinitive with *volver a* + place, which means "to go back to": *Zumbi volvió a Palmares* is not "he did it again". Object pronouns go before *volver* or at the end of the infinitive: *Lo volvieron a atacar* = *Volvieron a atacarlo*.
